p2 and p3 are both past the orange properties, so they cannot land on them this turn. Building to kill them would only pay off after a full orbit, roughly eight to twelve turns from now. p4 is currently at Water Works.

p4's roll from Water Works lands on Go to Jail, Pacific Avenue, North Carolina Avenue, Community Chest, Pennsylvania Avenue, Short Line, Chance, Park Place, Luxury Tax, Boardwalk, and GO. None of these spaces are orange properties.

Since p2, p3, and p4 are all past the orange spaces, none of them can land on them before my next turn. The only way someone could reach an orange property via a chance card would be by moving to a railroad, Illinois, or St. Charles, not directly to orange.

No chance card sends a player directly to an orange property, so no opponent will pay me orange rent before my next roll. Extra houses are therefore purely defensive and strategic investments for the future. I am now calculating my own landing spots from Community Chest: rolling 2 lands on Income Tax, while rolling 3 would hit Reading Railroad and cost p4 fifty dollars.

Rolling 9, 11, or 12 from Community Chest lands on St. Charles, States, and Virginia. These pink properties are dangerous if p3 has built houses on them. Rolling 4 would hit Oriental at p4's light-blue rent of six dollars. Rolling 10 would hit the Electric Utility for one hundred dollars.

The exact probabilities for rolling from Community Chest are now clear. The probability of landing on a pink property from Community Chest is roughly nineteen percent. The key question is whether p3 will spend five dollars on seven houses when I already have orange houses and they will eventually lap into me.

The smart path is four houses, leaving three hundred five dollars cash, or three houses, leaving four hundred five dollars cash. A three-house build also leaves them enough liquidity to survive. The orange properties only become a true kill trap once p3 has already spent cash on houses.

I will build three houses on each orange property for three hundred dollars and keep six hundred fifty-eight dollars cash. This matches my earlier plan exactly.

I have nine hundred fifty-eight dollars total. The six hundred fifty-eight dollar buffer covers Virginia at four houses, which would cost seven hundred dollars. p3 cannot afford four houses on Virginia because it costs twelve hundred dollars and they only have seven hundred five dollars.

A 4/3/3 build would leave only $558 cash, which is too low to survive the worst-case Virginia rent of $500. The three-house orange build is therefore the safer choice.

The past self had warned that leaving only fifty-eight dollars cash after paying the worst-case Virginia rent would be too fragile. The prior plan to cap orange houses at three each was meant to cover the highest hostile rent, but that warning assumed yellow properties were already at three houses. Yellow is currently at one house and p4 has only forty-six dollars cash, so a Marvin rent of eight hundred fifty dollars is not a realistic threat this cycle.

The three-house orange build leaves one hundred fifty-eight dollars cash after paying the worst-case Virginia rent of five hundred dollars. That buffer is comfortable and preserves all houses intact.

A four-house build would leave only fifty-eight dollars cash after the same rent. That is too fragile to survive another hit.

The extra house in a four-house build does not pay off before the risk window closes. I will roll into pink properties before any opponent can reach the oranges.

The $200 from passing GO raises the planned buffer to $658, which is better than originally intended. I will build three houses on each orange property now, then end my turn.
